device_identification.what_it_is: A balanced Mach-Zehnder interferometer nested inside an outer racetrack (stadium) loop. The loop connects to the MZI at its left and right vertices, so the two MZI arms plus the loop form a closed optical path (a loop-mirror / ring-loaded MZI).
device_identification.how_it_works: Light entering the loop is split by a 1->2 splitter at the left vertex into a top arm and a bottom arm. Each arm passes through a wide 'phase section' -- a solid rectangular block etched with two rectangular windows separated by a central bridge (a slotted/multimode phase-and-coupling region). The arms recombine at a mirror-image 2->1 combiner at the right vertex. The relative phase accrued in the two arms sets the interference; the surrounding stadium loop recirculates/reflects, making this a resonant interferometric element.
device_identification.symmetry: Mirror-symmetric about the vertical centerline (x=1.5um) and the horizontal centerline (y=2.75um).

function_knobs.guide_w: arm waveguide width -- sets single-mode confinement
function_knobs.arm_offset: half-separation of the two MZI arms (arm pitch) -- the interferometer split geometry
function_knobs.ps_len: phase-section length (x) -- the phase/coupling interaction length (MMI-like transfer length)
function_knobs.ps_h: phase-section transverse height -- multimode width of the slotted block
function_knobs.slot_gap / bridge_w: the etched-window gap and central bridge -- set the slot coupling
function_knobs.split_taper_len / split_tip_w: splitter/combiner taper length and tip width -- the 1->2 junction

calibration_note: Image is anisotropically scaled: x maps 3.0um->1551px (517 px/um), y maps 5.5um->780px (141.8 px/um). All feature coordinates were measured as fractions of the bbox and converted x_um=frac*3.0, y_um=frac*5.5, so the device is built at 3.0um (x) by 5.5um (y) and the rasterizer's anisotropic scale reproduces the 2:1 visual aspect.
primitives_note: Built from gf.components.rectangle, gf.components.ellipse (corner rounding), gf.components.taper (splitter wedges), gf.path.smooth+extrude (arms), gf.cross_section, and gf.boolean (loop annulus, etch windows). ellipse is used as a geometric primitive to render anisotropic (elliptical) corners forced by the x/y calibration mismatch. No gf.components device stencils (no mmi/coupler/etc.), no raw add_polygon.

iterations.change_made: Initial build: stadium (racetrack) loop via constant-width gf.Path extrude; splitter wedges; slotted phase sections (rect minus 2 windows); arms as sharp polyline extrudes.
Loop -> rounded-rectangle path (target has flat top/sides, not semicircular caps); replaced thin stems with fat splitter wedges (split_base_w=1.30).
Reduced ring_wall to 0.32 and smoothed arm S-bends (gf.path.smooth) to kill miter spikes. Revealed the anisotropy problem: a constant-width loop renders thin top/bottom, fat sides.

Rebuilt loop as boolean(outer_rect - inner_cavity_rect) with independent side (0.339) and top/bottom (0.517) wall thickness to absorb anisotropy. Straight walls now match; corners sharp (red outer / blue inner corners).
Rounded both outer and inner corners with elliptical corners (2 rects + 4 ellipses per rounded-rect). Initial radius guesses (outer 0.9/1.5, inner 0.55/0.95).

Fitted corner radii from the image corner curves: outer ellipse (0.9, 2.2), inner cavity ellipse (0.74, 1.57), ring_wall_x=0.31. IoU >= 0.85 reached; kept as honest best. (A follow-up wedge trim gave 0.8729 -- negligibly worse -- and was reverted.)
